title: Subject–Verb Agreement
description: Master subject-verb agreement for Grade 7: compound subjects, either/neither, collective and uncountable nouns, intervening phrases and titles — with practice and tests.

topics.title: Compound Subjects & Either/Neither
topics.concept:
When two subjects are joined by and, they usually take a plural verb:

  • Ram and Shyam are friends.
  • Exception: if the two form one idea, use singular — Bread and butter is my breakfast.

When subjects are joined by or, nor, either…or, neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject:

  • Either the teacher or the students are wrong. (nearer = students)
  • Neither the students nor the teacher is wrong. (nearer = teacher)

'Each', 'every', 'either', 'neither' as subjects are singular: Each of the boys is ready.

examples.problem: Choose: Neither the players nor the captain ___ (was/were) present.

recap: Subjects joined by or/nor → verb agrees with the nearer subject

topics.title: Intervening Phrases, Collective & Uncountable Nouns
topics.concept:
A phrase between the subject and the verb does not change the verb. Find the real subject and ignore the phrase.

  • The box of books is heavy. (not 'are')
  • The quality of the products is good.

Collective nouns (team, family, jury) usually take a singular verb when acting as one unit: The team has won. (Use a plural verb only when members act individually.)

Uncountable nouns and certain nouns plural in form but singular in meaning take a singular verb:

  • The news is good. Mathematics is easy. Water is precious.

A title or a single name is singular: "Oliver Twist" is a novel.

examples.solution: was — the subject is 'the list' (singular); 'of items' is an intervening phrase.
is — 'news' is singular though it ends in -s.

recap: Ignore phrases between subject and verb (the box of books is…)
Collective nouns acting as one → singular verb (the team has)
news, mathematics, water etc. take a singular verb

questions.q: 'Either the dog or the cats ___ hungry.'
Spot the error: 'The number of accidents have increased.'
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb → 'has increased'.

questions.q: Choose: 'Not only the students but also the teacher ___ excited.'
questions.explanation: With 'not only … but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'teacher' → 'is'.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'Many a student have failed the exam.'
questions.explanation: 'Many a + singular noun' takes a singular verb → 'has'.

questions.q: Fill in: 'Three-fourths of the work ___ done.'
questions.explanation: A fraction agrees with the noun after 'of'; 'work' is uncountable → 'is'.

questions.q: Choose: 'The jury ___ divided in their opinions.'
questions.explanation: When members act individually, the collective noun takes a plural verb → 'are'.

questions.q: Rearrange: 'is / of / one / friends / my / coming'
options: One of my friends is coming.
One of my friends are coming.
One of my friend is coming.
My friends one of is coming.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: 'Either you or I ___ mistaken.'

outcomes: State the basic rule of subject–verb agreement
Use the right verb with either/neither and collective nouns
Ignore intervening phrases between subject and verb
Treat titles and uncountable nouns as singular

intro.en: Subject–verb agreement means the verb must match its subject in number: a singular subject takes a singular verb, a plural subject takes a plural verb. "The dog barks" but "The dogs bark." It sounds simple — until phrases sneak in between the subject and the verb.
intro.hi: कर्ता-क्रिया मेल (Subject–Verb Agreement) का अर्थ है कि क्रिया अपने कर्ता से वचन में मेल खाए: एकवचन कर्ता के साथ एकवचन क्रिया, बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ बहुवचन क्रिया। "The dog barks" पर "The dogs bark।" यह आसान लगता है — जब तक बीच में कोई वाक्यांश न आ जाए।

real_life.situation:
You proofread a notice:

Draft: The list of winners are on the board.

Fixed: The list of winners is on the board.
real_life.why: The real subject is 'the list' (singular), not 'winners'. The phrase 'of winners' is just extra information. Spotting the true subject is the key skill of this chapter.

quick_test.q: With 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with:
quick_test.explanation: With or/nor, the verb agrees with the nearer (last) subject.

rearrangement.jumbled: is / of / the / box / books / heavy
rearrangement.answer: The box of books is heavy.

right: singular verb (and = one idea? no, plural)

reading.passage: The committee of teachers has decided to hold a fair. The news is exciting. Neither the students nor the principal is against it. A list of activities has been prepared, and the box of prizes is ready. Mathematics, science and art are all part of the show, and every class is going to take part.

questions.q: Why is 'has decided' singular in 'The committee … has decided'?
questions.answer: 'committee' is a collective noun acting as one unit, so it takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Find a sentence where an intervening phrase could trap you.
questions.answer: 'A list of activities has been prepared' — the subject is 'list' (singular), not 'activities'.
'every' makes the subject singular, so the verb is 'is'.

speaking: Each of the boys has a uniform.
Neither of the answers is correct.
Mathematics is easier than I thought.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences using a collective noun, an intervening phrase, 'each', 'neither … nor', and an uncountable noun like 'news' — with correct agreement.
writing.example: The class is ready. Each of the students has a desk. The news is good.

options: A number of students is absent.

challenge.q: Identify the error: 'The quality of the answers were excellent.'

challenge.explanation: A measured distance acts as one unit → singular 'is'.

revision: Singular subject → singular verb; plural subject → plural verb
Subjects joined by 'and' → plural (unless they form one idea)
or/nor → verb agrees with the nearer subject
Ignore phrases between subject and verb (the box of pens is…)
news, mathematics, each, neither, collective nouns → singular verb
